subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — recap & next steps

Jamie — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the evaluation.

Recap (what I heard):
- Workload: multi-tenant inference for ACME Chat Assist (LLM prompts + embeddings for similarity).
- Peak: ~700-1,000 concurrent requests during business hours; burst to ~2k for product launches.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for short-form generate; p99 budgeted at ~500ms.
- Data: customer PII filtered upstream; however, data residency + audit logs are required for compliance.
- Priority: predictable capacity for production, cost transparency, and a tested failover path to our hyperscaler stack during peaks.

Primary evaluation questions you raised:
1) How does Redwood Dedicated compare to hyperscaler reserved GPU instances (cost + capacity guarantees)?
2) Can Dedicated support burst capacity without sacrificing the committed throughput?
3) What tests should we run to validate latency, cost, and graceful degradation?

Proposed next steps / POC scope:
- Test matrix: Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) vs Hyperscaler reserved instances (ACME-managed AWS/Azure).
  - Benchmarks: throughput (QPS at 50/500/2000 concurrent), tail latency (p95/p99), cold-start behavior for key model sizes, and cost per 1M tokens.
  - Reliability: failover test where traffic is shifted between Redwood Dedicated and the hyperscaler variant to validate session continuity and fallback latency.
  - Operational checks: autoscaling behavior, cache warming (KV cache), and network egress patterns.
- Timeline: 3-week POC after access is granted. Week 1: perf baseline + tooling integration. Week 2: stress & failover. Week 3: run production-like traffic and validate cost numbers.
- Deliverables: benchmark report, recommended config (batching / quantization profile), and a mutual action plan (MAP) with acceptance criteria.

What we need from ACME to start:
- Test credentials / sandbox access or sample payloads (we can also replay captured traffic if you prefer).
- A short PO/authorization to provision a reserved Dedicated pool (we can start sizing with provisional numbers if you want to delay PO).
- Security contacts for SOC2 evidence and network egress requirements.

Attachments: I attached a short comparison doc (Redwood_vs_Hyperscaler_Comparison.pdf) and a suggested POC scope sheet (acme-poc-scope.xlsx).

Proposed calendar slots for kickoff (PT):
- Tue 7/6 10:00-11:00
- Wed 7/7 14:00-15:00

If you confirm one of those, we’ll lock in Marissa (Solutions Eng) and Rishi (SRE/sales engineer) to run the technical kickoff and sizing.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

— Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — great summary. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

1) Pricing model: can you confirm whether Dedicated is fundamentally a committed monthly fee (reserved capacity) vs metered overage billing? We need clarity for procurement.
2) Burst capacity: you mentioned burst support — is that an add-on or built into the reserved pool? How fast can it ramp (seconds/minutes)?
3) Security evidence: please include SOC2 + network diagram in the kickoff packet so our security team can triage quickly.

Procurement has asked for estimated monthly committed spend for the POC so they can provision a PO (we don’t yet need a full contract). Can you provide a ballpark number for the 3-week POC (reserved pool sized for 1k steady, 2k burst)?

We can do Tue 7/6 10:00 PT — that works for me and I’ll loop in our infra lead if the calendar invite goes out.

— Jamie

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>, security-team@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Hyperscaler eval — recap & next steps

Jamie — thanks, great questions. Short answers below and I’ll have Marissa follow up with a sizing + cost worksheet before EOD.

1) Pricing model: Redwood Dedicated is a committed monthly fee for reserved capacity (covers baseline throughput and a fixed number of vGPU-hours). We do support metered overage at a pre-agreed rate for bursts beyond the commitment; overage pricing is transparent and applied hourly. For the POC we can do a short-term committed reservation (monthly pro-rated) to give you capacity guarantees without requiring a long-term contract.

2) Burst capacity: built-in option — customers can configure burst tiers. Burst ramp is typically seconds-to-minutes depending on model size and whether new nodes need to spin up; for warmed pools (with KV cache primed) we can handle sub-30s scale-ups for additional queued capacity. For strict hard SLOs we recommend a small buffer on committed baseline and a modest burst tier to avoid p99 regressions.

3) Security evidence: noted. Attaching our SOC2 summary and a network diagram to the kickoff packet (Marissa will include).

Estimated POC cost (very rough for procurement):
- Committed reserved pool (pro-rated for 3 weeks) sized for 1k steady / 2k burst: ~$12k-18k USD (depends on model family & quantization).
- Add-on: temporary burst buffer (policy-based) + extra vGPU-hours for stress testing: ~$3k-5k USD.

If that range looks fine to procurement, we’ll provision a pro-rated reservation for the POC and proceed. I’ll send a formal MAP with acceptance criteria + the DocuSign PO link once procurement confirms.

Next steps (agreed):
- I’ll share the MAP + SOC2 summary + network diagram (Marissa).
- Marissa will run the technical kickoff on Tue 7/6 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow).
- Rishi will prepare a test harness and suggested payloads; if you can share sample traces, we’ll incorporate them into the baseline.

Anything else you want on the kickoff agenda? If not I’ll lock the invite and loop in sales ops to generate the pro-rated PO link.

— Markus
